insights.insight: Static source can expose a plausible state path without establishing that the integrated product actually exhibits the defect; route to the cheapest integrated discriminator before granting build permission.
insights.promotion_reason: This is already encoded by Neta's discrimination-before-redesign, reality-floor and permission rules; the batch adds transfer evidence, not a new rule.

insights.insight: Independent evidence about a neighboring bug or the same component can support a failure family without confirming the exact mechanism under adjudication.
insights.promotion_reason: Needs counterexamples, a falsifiable adjudication gate and unseen HOLDOUT success before becoming a benchmark or Neta rule. OSS-0005 is HOLDOUT and is not used to promote or modify this insight until the holdout wave closes.

insights.insight: A suspicious timing workaround is not itself permission to refactor; first reproduce the event mechanism with and without the workaround.
insights.promotion_reason: Single case, no neighbor control, no positive control and no HOLDOUT evidence.

insights.insight: A repository can establish exactly what the product does while remaining unable to establish that the behavior is a defect; when the unresolved question is intended interaction/configuration policy, route to OWNER instead of converting implementation certainty into build permission.
insights.promotion_reason: This is already encoded by Neta's separation of evidence, authority and permission. Two unfamiliar TRAIN cases add transfer evidence but do not justify a new prompt/rule.

decision_modes.note: OWNER routing appeared in two TRAIN cases, breaking the all-DISCRIMINATE pattern. BUILD_READY and FIELD_STOP remain absent.

failure_families.note: Batch 002 added one authority-boundary family, but it maps to an already-canonical Neta distinction rather than a new rule.

authority_boundaries.note: OWNER appeared in two TRAIN cases; ENVIRONMENT appeared in one HOLDOUT case and is aggregate-only until the holdout wave closes.

baseline_decision_deltas.note: Two new TRAIN cases produced surviving restraint deltas by separating implementation fact from product-policy authority.
